text: Hello boys and girls, how are you?I'm Astrid, welcome back to my class.Please get your students' book and worksheet ready.In the last period, we talked about our dream vacations.We talked about what some cities or countries are famous for.What you would like to do and to see there.Today, we are going to talk about a city or a country we've been to.Do you still remember the last place you went on holiday?Where did you go?What did you do there?Did you have a good time?Take a few moments to think about these questions.Then talk to yourself aloud.Emma, can you share with us the last place you went on holiday?I went to Helsinki, Finland last summer holiday and enjoyed myself there.There are many small towns and churches.I visited an old town called Pervo, a wonderland for children and a church made of rock, which was so cool for us to stay in.I also tried some Finnish snacks, totally different from ours, but I loved them.I had great fun there.Oh, it seemed to be a nice experience.Evangel, tell us about your last trip.Last summer vacation, I had a trip in Japan.I traveled in Tokyo, Osaka and many other places, but the night view in Kobe really impressed me.I will never forget the moment when all the lights were on and the whole city shone brightly.It was so beautiful.I wish I could go back there again.Wow, what an unforgettable moment.Thank you for sharing with us.When you are traveling, you enjoy beautiful scenery and taste delicious food.How do you share your happiness with the ones you love?By the Internet.True, we live in a world that is amazingly connected.We have got different ways to stay in touch with our friends and family members wherever we are.However, with everyone sending email or instant messages, do you want to do something to make your loved ones feel special?What about writing a postcard?Sending someone a postcard about your travel will allow the receivers to remember how you took the time to write out your experiences.And they can hold that love in their hands.Postcards give a picture and story from another place.Look, this is a postcard.What can you see on the front of the postcard?Pictures of a hotel, I guess.On the back of the postcard, you will find that it has been divided into two parts.The right side is meant for the postcard address.The left side is basically meant to carry the message, the writer's story.Read the message carefully and answer the four questions orally.Who is the postcard from?Yes, it is from Amy, and Amy writes the postcard to John.When did Amy arrive?Can you see the date in the top left corner of the postcard?12th JulyAnd Amy arrived yesterday.So she arrived on 11th July.You are right.What is she doing now?She is now staying at the hotel in the picture.What is she going to do tomorrow?She is going to build a waterfall in the forest tomorrow.What elements does a postcard usually include?Please finish task 1 on your worksheet.Label the postcard with the words in the box.Here are the answers.A postcard usually includes date, greeting, message, signature, stamp, and address.Whose address?The receiver's address.The postcard's address.Write the receiver's address on the right side of the postcard.This includes their full name, address, area code, province or city, and country.How can we write the address?Room number, floor, building, housing estate or street address, city, and then country.Does this postcard include six elements?It doesn't include a date, but it has a P.is the short form of post script.A post script is a short additional message you can write at the very end of a postcard or letter after you've signed your name.Write P.and then your message.Let's take a close look at the postcard.Who writes the postcard?Guy, Jackie, and Mia's parents.How do the parents begin the postcard?By saying the name of the postcard.By saying Dear Guy, Jackie, and Mia.Actually, they are giving a greeting.A greeting will make the person you write to feel special and appreciated.It also gives the postcard a heartfelt feel.Why do the parents write the sentences in the green box?Because they want to tell the receivers where they are and what they are doing.What tense is used in the sentences in the red box?The simple past tense, because these are the things they did.Why do they use be going to to describe the things in the blue box?To show that these are the things they plan to do.In other words, these are future plans.How do they end the postcard?By saying We miss you.At the end of the postcard come their signatures and a post-script.Here are some sentences from postcards.Mark each expression P for talking about the past,F for talking about the future,or T for typical postcard expressions, which means the expressions often used in a postcard.That is task 2 on your worksheet.A piece of cake for you, right?Let's look at the first one.What does wish you were here mean?It means I wish you could be here, enjoying all the nice things together with me.It usually appears in the closing part of a postcard.What other phrases can we use to close a postcard?We can also say best wishes, I miss you, see you soon, etc.Tell the persons that you miss them or that you've been thinking about them during your travels,and that you're excited to see them again.Your thoughts of the other persons will make them feel loved.Now, let's practice.Task 3.Complete the postcard text with the expressions from the box.Let's check the answers.After reading three postcards, can you tell me what holiday postcards have in common?Right, holiday postcards have three main characteristics.They are short, positive, even if it's raining.And have predictable message in their content.The message usually includes three parts.Part 1, present state.Part 2, past activities.Part 3, future plans.For part 1, you can start with a greeting and a sentence about where you are and what the weather is like.This will make the receivers feel closer to you.You can also express your first impression of the place.In this part, we often use the simple present tense and the present continuous tense.For example, you can say,Hi, hello, dear, I'm having an incredible time here in Egypt.I'm staying in the capital city of Cairo.It is very hot and sunny here.London is like our city in a way.The food and many other things are similar.I'm having such a fun time in Australia.I'm doing a lot of travelling while I'm here.It's so nice to be in a warm place.I love it here.The sky and the sea are blue and the beach is beautiful.Let's move on to part 2, past activities.In this part, you should write about what you did.Use the simple past tense.Let's take the holiday at the beach as an example.Suppose you are spending your holiday at the beach.What fun things could you do?List the beach activities you can think of in your notebook.What have you written down, Jennifer?We could do some activities like swimming, surfing and yawning.We could also play some games, such as beach volleyball, tossing a frisbee over the sand or in the water.Good idea!Anymore?Awesome?I prefer to make sand castles or collect seashells on the beach.Relaxing and sunbathing are good choices too.But what I want to do most is to watch the beautiful sunrise and sunset.Good!Anything to add, Evan?For some beaches, fishing is permitted.We could look for a fishing tour and learn to cast a line.What's more, water sports like snorkeling and scuba diving are more and more popular among young people.Thank you.Well, we have gathered so much information.Next, suppose you are spending your holiday at the beach.Write a couple of sentences about the things you did in your notebook.Remember, the activities are usually arranged in time order.Here's an example.Now, it's your turn.David, could you share your writing with us?Today, I went to Boundee Beach.It was very beautiful.I went to Boundee Beach.I went surfing.I think I need some more practice as I kept falling in the water.Wow, you must have been to Australia.Boundee Beach is well-known all over the world.Besides the beach, there are many other interesting places to go.I'll show you three pictures representing three countries with their own features.Please guess what they are.Bingo!Egypt, Japan and Italy.This time, please brainstorm the things you could do in any one of the countries.Here are some suggested things to do.Pick one of the three countries to write a couple of sentences in your notebook about what you did in that country.Which tense should you use?Write the simple past tense.Evangel, which country did you write about?Yesterday, we went to visit Mount Fuji.We were lucky to see the mountain top clearly.Today, I went sightseeing around Kyoto in Aki Mono, Japan's traditional clothing.Can't wait to share the photos with you.Oh, you wrote about Japan.Well done.Emma, it's your turn to share with us.Yesterday, I went to visit the Colosseum in Rome.It was a great historical relic.Then I made a wish by throwing a coin into the Travi Fountain.Today, I was in Florence, enjoying the masterpieces of Italian art at the Ofsi Gallery.Wow, you must be a history and art lover.In a postcard, after talking about the things we did, we usually end the postcard with our future plans.That is the third part.Write about the things you are going to do.Here are three examples.How can you make your postcard writing vivid and interesting?The key is to add your own feelings in your writing.If possible, add some details too.Let's look at these sentences.Pay close attention to the part highlighted in red.So far, we have finished discussing the main part of a postcard.And I believe you have had your own ideas on how to write a postcard.Here's an example for you.Read it by yourself.Next, it's your turn to have a try.Suppose you are having a holiday abroad.Write a postcard to your best friend.After finishing writing, use the checklist to decide whether you have included all the important elements and whether you have used the right tense.Let's look at the main part of a postcard.If possible, use the checklist to decide whether you have included all the important elements and whether you have used the right tense.This is a postcard written by Emma.Does the postcard include all the important elements?Does Emma use the right tense?Does she express her feelings?At the beginning of the postcard, she expresses her love for the city.What about details?She says she waved to lots of people on the riverbank.And she also describes the appearance of the Sphinx.But she made four mistakes in using the definite article the and conjunctions.Can you help her correct the mistakes?Let's do it together.I'm staying in the capital city.I sail down the Nile.Although the Sphinx looks like a big cat or lion.Although and but cannot be used in the same sentence.Here we can delete but.Tomorrow, I'm going to the Egyptian Museum.When you are practicing writing, always pay attention to the uses of articles and conjunctions.Finally, some tips for you.Pick out a postcard that represents you or your travels.Date your postcard.This acts as a reminder to the receiver later on when he or she goes through the postcard.Be sure to give yourself enough space and plan what you are going to write.You don't want to run out of space in the middle of a thought.Do not write about anything too personal.Remember, the information on the back of the postcard can be read by others.Make your writing as clear and legible as possible.If you are not sure what you are going to write.Do not complain in your postcard, even if you are having a terrible time.So much for today.As for your homework, please revise the postcard in today's lesson.You also need to complete some exercises on your workbook.Have a good day.See you.
